chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-Luʾluʾī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abī al-Miʿzā Ḥumayd ibn al-Muthannā, from ʿImrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, that he asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a travelling man when he enters into...
...the salat (prayer) with the residents. He said: Then let him perform his salat (prayer), then give salām, and make the last two as supererogatory prayer.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the last two, referring to the remaining two rakʿahs
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: traveller, the person subject to shortened prayer rulings
key_terms.سُبْحَةً: supererogatory prayer, counted as voluntary rather than obligatory
key_terms.فَلْيُصَلِّ: let him pray, an instruction indicating the ruling
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he gives salām, ending his obligatory prayer

ai.seo_question: How should a traveller pray when following a resident Imam in congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a traveller praying behind residents in congregational salat (prayer). It indicates that after completing his own shortened obligation, he gives salām, and the remaining two rakʿahs are counted as supererogatory prayer.
